prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for truck accidents — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your case and which lawyer has the experience, resources and chemistry that fit your needs. I can help you find strong candidates, but first here are practical things to know and steps to take.

What to look for in a truck‑accident lawyer
- Significant experience with commercial truck cases (different law, federal regs, complex liability).
- Trial experience and a record of large verdicts/settlements in trucking matters.
- Resources: investigators, accident reconstruction experts, medical experts, and ability to handle litigation against well‑funded trucking companies/insurers.
- Good reputation: peer reviews (Martindale‑Hubbell), Super Lawyers, AVVO, state/local bar referrals, membership in groups such as the Texas Trial Lawyers Association or American Association for Justice.
- Clear fee structure (contingency), communication style, and availability.
- Willingness to promptly preserve evidence (black box, logbooks, driver records), and to obtain a prompt independent investigation.

Time sensitivity and practical notes
- Texas statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the accident date (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §16.003) — exceptions exist, so act quickly.
- Trucking companies often purge evidence quickly; the sooner you consult a lawyer the better.
- Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency fees often range ~33–40% plus litigation costs.

How to find strong Dallas attorneys
- Contact the Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA) or the Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral service.
- Check attorney ratings on Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers, and AVVO, and read client reviews.
- Ask for attorneys who regularly handle federal and state trucking cases and who can provide references and sample verdicts/settlements.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases involving the trucking company’s black box (E‑log), hours‑of‑service violations, and driver drug/alcohol testing?
- Do you have accident reconstruction and medical experts you use regularly?
- What is your contingency fee and how are expenses handled?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day, and how will you communicate updates?

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of well‑reviewed Dallas truck‑accident attorneys (I can pull current listings if you want me to search now).
- Help draft an email or phone script to contact attorneys for consultations.
- Review details of your case (date, location, injuries, involved parties) and recommend next steps.

Which would you prefer? If you want attorney suggestions, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas and any special needs (e.g., catastrophic injury, wrongful death, multiple parties) so I can tailor recommendations.
